title: Sampling: head, tail and parent-based
summary: Keeping every trace is expensive. Head sampling decides at the start, tail sampling after the end, and parent-based sampling keeps traces whole.

steps.title: Decide early, or decide late
body: A busy service produces far more spans than anyone reads, and backends bill by volume. **Sampling** keeps a subset.
- **Head sampling** decides when the root span starts, in the SDK: `TraceIdRatioBased(0.1)` keeps 10% of traces. Cheap (dropped
spans are never even recorded), but blind: it keeps errors and slow requests at the same 10% as everything else.
- **Parent-based**: a span with a remote parent follows the `sampled` flag in `traceparent`. Only the root decides; everyone
downstream follows, so a kept trace is complete. `ParentBased(root: ...)` is the SDK default (`parentbased_always_on`).
- **Tail sampling** decides after the trace is complete, in a Collector that sees all its spans: keep every error, every trace
slower than 1 s, and 5% of the rest. It costs memory (traces are buffered for `decision_wait`) and every span of a trace must
Metrics are not sampled: they count every request whatever the traces keep, which is why you alert on metrics. Below, 1 000
traces with 1% errors and 2% slow ones. Compare 10% head sampling with tail sampling at the same storage cost.

otelviz.caption: Dots are traces in arrival order; ringed ones failed (red) or were slow (orange). A real tail sampler's policies: status_code, latency, probabilistic.

steps.prompt: The shop samples 100% at the root. Inventory is configured with `traceidratio` 0.2 (not parent-based). What do you see in Jaeger?
options: Most shop traces have no inventory spans: inventory ignores the sampled flag and records only a fifth of the traces
Every trace is complete, because the trace id is the same
Inventory's spans appear in separate traces of their own
Nothing changes: samplers only apply to metrics
steps.explain: A non-parent-based sampler makes its own decision. The shop keeps the trace, inventory drops its part: a trace with holes, exactly the lab's task 5. Fix: `parentbased_traceidratio` (or `parentbased_always_on`) everywhere except, if you want, the root.

steps.title: How a ratio sampler decides
body: A ratio sampler must make the **same** decision for the same trace in every service, without talking to the others. So it decides
from the trace id itself, which is random: read part of the id as a number and keep the trace when that number is below
`ratio × maximum`. The .NET SDK's `TraceIdRatioBasedSampler` reads the first 8 bytes as a 64-bit integer.
Newer specs make this exact across languages: W3C Trace Context Level 2 marks trace ids whose last 7 bytes are random (flag `02`), and
OpenTelemetry's consistent probability sampling compares those 56 bits with a threshold it records in `tracestate` (`ot=th:...`),
so a backend can count what each kept trace stands for.

steps.prompt: This is the decision rule of the next exercise. Which trace ids does a 25% sampler keep?
code: bool Keep(string traceId, double ratio) => ulong.Parse(traceId[..16], System.Globalization.NumberStyles.HexNumber) / 18446744073709551616.0 < ratio;
steps.explain: `0x1fff...` is 1/8 of the 64-bit range, under 0.25: kept. `0x4000...` is exactly 1/4: not under it. `0xc0ff...` is about 75%. Every service applying the same rule to the same id agrees.

steps.title: ParentBased(TraceIdRatioBased)
prompt: Write `bool Sample(string traceId, bool? parentSampled, bool parentIsRemote, double ratio)`, the SDK default with a ratio root:
- with a parent (`parentSampled` not null), follow it: return `parentSampled.Value` (both for a remote parent, from `traceparent`,
and a local one, `parentIsRemote` only matters for configuring the two separately, which you do not do here);
- without a parent (a root span), keep the trace when the first 16 hex digits of the trace id, read as an unsigned 64-bit number,
divided by 2^64 (`18446744073709551616.0`) is **below** `ratio`. `ratio` 0 keeps nothing, 1 keeps everything.
starter: bool Sample(string traceId, bool? parentSampled, bool parentIsRemote, double ratio)
solution: bool Sample(string traceId, bool? parentSampled, bool parentIsRemote, double ratio)
if (parentSampled is bool parent) return parent;
hints: `if (parentSampled is bool parent) return parent;` handles every child span.
template: Dojo.Eq("a sampled remote parent is followed", true, Sample("ffffffffffffffff0000000000000001", true, true, 0.01));
Dojo.Eq("an unsampled parent is followed", false, Sample("0000000000000001ffffffffffffffff", false, true, 1.0));
Dojo.Eq("a local parent is followed too", true, Sample("ffffffffffffffff0000000000000001", true, false, 0.0));
Dojo.Eq("root under the ratio: kept", true, Sample("1fffffffffffffff0000000000000001", null, false, 0.25));
Dojo.Eq("root at the boundary: dropped", false, Sample("4000000000000000ffffffffffffffff", null, false, 0.25));
Dojo.Eq("ratio 1 keeps a high id", true, Sample("efffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff", null, false, 1.0));
Dojo.Eq("ratio 0 keeps nothing", false, Sample("0000000000000001ffffffffffffffff", null, false, 0.0));
var dojoKept = dojoIds.Count(id => Sample(id, null, false, 0.1));
Dojo.Check("about 10% of 2 000 roots are kept", dojoKept is > 150 and < 250, "kept " + dojoKept);
Dojo.Check("two services agree on every trace", dojoIds.All(id => Sample(id, null, false, 0.1) == Sample(id, null, true, 0.1)), "");

steps.prompt: Where is this decided: the SDK at the root (head) or a Collector after the trace ends (tail)?
items: keep every trace that contains an error
keep every trace slower than 2 s end to end
keep all traces of tenant `acme`, 1% of the others
drop spans before they are even recorded, to save CPU
steps.explain: Anything that depends on what happened (an error, the total duration, an attribute set late) needs the whole trace: tail. Head sampling only knows what is true when the root starts.
